- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward spikes (e.g., +3–5% in 1–2 days) — especially after negative sentiment turns positive; apply “overshoot correction” by +1–2% in the immediate next period.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 1–3 periods — if sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1), adjust forecast to align with 2–3-period mean reversion trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility — especially after sentiment shifts to positive; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive positive entries, model tends to overcorrect downward — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in the 1st–3rd period of the 30-day window.
